solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 11 across, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: Stone dry in middle of deep lab drawer

indicators.note: the dry letters sit inside the pair taken from 'deep'
asks for the central letters of 'deep'

blocks.note: a pip is a fruit stone
the two central letters of dEEp
TT = teetotal, i.e. off the drink

explanation.surface: A stone left sitting dry at the bottom of a deep drawer in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' reads as furniture, but here it is something that draws: a pipette draws liquid up into its tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipette is the lab tube used to draw up measured amounts of liquid.

clue.text: Still reward nurses Charlie provided

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold something close, so PAY holds C and IF

blocks.note: C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone still rewarding a nurse called Charlie, provided conditions are met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' opens the clue looking like an adverb, but it is the verb: to still someone is to calm them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'still' here is the verb meaning to calm or quieten, as you still a crying child.

clue.text: Keep going over part of Sister Eve’s repertoire

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'over' turns the letters upward, reading them backwards
says the answer is a portion of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of sistER through EVE'S to the start of REPertoire

explanation.surface: A nun, Sister Eve, keeps working through her musical repertoire.
explanation.walkthrough: Repertoire invites thoughts of hymns; the answer is simply lying backwards across the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to carry on steadily in spite of setbacks.

clue.text: Worn item of leather crowning king spinning toy

indicators.note: in a down clue, TAN sits on top of K like a crown

blocks.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A leather crown placed on a king who is playing with a spinning top.
explanation.walkthrough: A tank top is a sleeveless knitted pullover in British usage, a vest-like garment worn over a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A vague but fair definition: any garment is a worn item, and this one is a sleeveless pullover.

clue.text: Reminder backing musician needs piano for service

indicators.note: going backwards, so CUE becomes EUC
to need something is to lack it, so the musician is without P

blocks.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder
HARPIST without P, the musical abbreviation for piano

explanation.surface: A prompt backing a musician in a church service who needs a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs' reads as wanting something added, but here it means lacking it, so the piano comes out rather than going in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian service of Holy Communion.

clue.text: Career police officers returned for drink

indicators.note: sent back, so the letters read in reverse

blocks.note: to career is to rush along, to race

explanation.surface: Career police officers came back from duty for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like an adjective describing the officers, but it is the verb meaning to hurtle along.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Term read labouriously letter by letter

blocks.note: a term is a period of time, such as a stint in office
to make out a word one letter at a time

explanation.surface: Someone slowly sounding out a term, one letter at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: A spell is a period or term (a spell in office); to spell is also to make out words slowly letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a stretch or term of time, and to spell out a word is to read it letter by letter.

clue.text: Show of protest jerk makes popular

blocks.note: a demo is a demonstration, a protest march
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A protest stunt by some jerk that somehow wins public favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' reads as an insult for a person, but it means a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of or for the ordinary people, popular.

clue.text: Craft store’s focus is encapsulated by wicker

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre letter
held inside, like a capsule

blocks.note: cane is the material of wicker furniture

explanation.surface: A craft shop whose centrepiece is a wicker display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as handicraft beside the store, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft is a general word for any boat, and this is a light paddled one.

clue.text: Assessed spin of wheels manufactured at Dorset

indicators.note: made up anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car made at a Dorset plant is taken out for an assessed drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is a county in south-west England. The long definition describes the thing itself: a road test is a drive taken to judge a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test is a trial drive in which a vehicle is assessed.

clue.text: Register regulars in cohort on river catching cold

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals from the words that follow
the river holds the C inside it

blocks.note: the Nile, the river of Egypt
C = cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A register of the regulars in a group living by a river who have caught colds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a joining word, but it belongs to the letters being sampled: CoHoRtOn gives CHRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'register' is the verb meaning to put on record, as a historian does.

clue.text: Divine food articles with one reflecting on end of veganism

indicators.note: mirrored, so one of the two ANs reads backwards
in an across clue, placed after the final letter of 'veganism'
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Vegan-friendly divine food, with a few articles reflecting on the end of veganism.
explanation.walkthrough: Manna is the food God sent the Israelites in the wilderness. 'Articles with one' gives AN plus AN, and it is the second that is reflected.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna is the food from heaven in the Book of Exodus.

clue.text: Navy paper general inscribes

indicators.note: the general's name is written inside the paper

blocks.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A general signing his name on a naval document.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT (Financial Times) is a British newspaper; it and Lee are both standard crossword stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nation's whole body of warships can be called either.

clue.text: 100 per cent of lotion’s lost in distribution

indicators.note: 's = has, so the lotion has lost the letters that follow

explanation.surface: The whole bottle of lotion lost somewhere during delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: The lotion is OINTMENT, and 'in' is literal: it is the pair of letters it loses.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the act of sharing something out, as in the allotting of shares.

clue.text: Dire prospects affected group’s solidarity

indicators.note: changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bleak prospects have hit a team's morale.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is persuasive: dire prospects really would affect morale, which is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit de corps is the shared pride and loyalty that holds a group together.

clue.text: Snake tailing delta fish reducing in number

indicators.note: following behind, so WIND comes after D

blocks.note: D is delta in the NATO alphabet
to snake is to wind, as a road does
the ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A snake following fish in a river delta whose numbers are falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' reads as the reptile, but it is the verb meaning to wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwindling means shrinking steadily in size or number.

clue.text: Did up tank Feds uncovered south of city

indicators.note: with the covering outer letters stripped off
in a down clue, below the city

blocks.note: a vat is a large tank

explanation.surface: The Feds found a tank somewhere south of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' suggests the Feds exposed something, but it strips the first and last letters from their name.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Did up' is the British idiom for refurbished, as you do up an old house.

clue.text: New split within diocese about Paulinian missives?

indicators.note: made new, so the letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go inside the diocese
turned about, so SEE reads backwards

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A fresh split in a diocese over the letters of St Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: St Paul's epistles are the best known, but not the only ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistles of Paul are the letters he wrote to early churches.

clue.text: Aristocrat bored by withdrawn assistant medic

indicators.note: drilled into, so the assistant goes inside
pulled back, so the letters read in reverse

explanation.surface: A snooty aristocrat is bored by an introverted assistant doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' reads as weary, but it means pierced.
explanation.definitionFit: A paediatrician is a doctor specialising in children.

clue.text: Get better unscripted comedy on tablet

indicators.note: in a down clue, IMPROV sits on top of E

explanation.surface: An improv comic performing while on pills.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a patient or a skill making progress.

clue.text: National Rail is struggling to save energy

indicators.note: in difficulty, so the letters are rearranged
to save something is to keep it safe, and here the jumbled letters keep E held within them

explanation.surface: The national rail network is struggling to cut its energy use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National Rail' reads as the British train operator, but 'National' alone is the definition: a citizen of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'national' as a noun means a citizen, and this is a citizen of one particular country.

clue.text: Deprive Soviet periodically fed by sailor

indicators.note: at regular intervals: every other letter
the sailor is put inside, like food

explanation.surface: A Soviet regime that deprives people is fed by a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' plays against the definition: the starving are the ones not fed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually of food, but also more broadly, as in starved of attention.

clue.text: Different females keeping record dated in pen

indicators.note: holding the record inside

blocks.note: two different words for female: SHE and F
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Various women keep an old record in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' reads as an anagram signal, but it means two distinct symbols for female: SHE and F.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is any enclosure for animals, and this is the one built for a flock.

clue.text: Opposing players finally offer to school recruit

indicators.note: the last letter of each word

blocks.note: East and North sit on opposite sides at bridge
last letters of offeR tO schooL

explanation.surface: Rival sides offer places to a school recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge, North–South play East–West, so East and North are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to sign someone up as a member or student.

clue.text: Composition and the like written up in books

indicators.note: in a down clue, written upwards, so reversed
'in' used literally: the reversed letters are put inside the abbreviation for books

explanation.surface: A composition and similar works catalogued in books.
explanation.walkthrough: An octet here is a piece of music for eight players.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a musical composition for eight instruments.

clue.text: Enthral experienced scientific institute member?

blocks.note: RI = the Royal Institution, a London science body
the question mark flags the whole as a playful picture of a veteran RI member

explanation.surface: A veteran member of a science institute holds an audience spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Experienced scientific institute member' is a single cryptic picture: an RI vet.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet someone is to hold their attention completely, to enthral.

clue.text: Vessel on lake is broad and slow

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed after L

explanation.surface: A boat on a lake that is wide and moving slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Largo is a musical tempo marking; the surface's sluggish broad vessel sits right beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction meaning broad and slow.

clue.text: Quarter of spruce trees flourished

indicators.note: waved about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In one part of the forest, the spruce trees have thrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' reads as a tree beside 'trees', but it is the adjective meaning smart. A term can be called a trimester or a quarter in some academic calendars.
explanation.definitionFit: Some academic years divide into terms called trimesters or quarters.

clue.text: Outstanding second romance colonist devours

indicators.note: swallows, so the colonist goes around the romance

blocks.note: to romance is to tell fanciful stories, to lie

explanation.surface: A remarkable second romance swallows up a settler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' looks like a noun for a love affair, but it is the verb meaning to invent stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent, standing out.

clue.text: Cook close to breaking sieve

indicators.note: a close is an ending, so the close to a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve

explanation.surface: A cook on the verge of smashing a sieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'nearly', but it asks for the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To griddle is to cook on a griddle, a flat iron plate.
